title: MCP Transports — stdio vs Streamable HTTP vs SSE Migration

questions.question: How does the HTTP handler treat an initialize request from an unapproved evil origin?
options: It returns HTTP 403 before dispatching JSON-RPC
It mints a session and returns 200
It accepts the request only when the body is empty
It converts the origin to localhost
questions.explanation: _require_origin checks the exact/prefix allowlist first, so an evil origin receives 403 and cannot create a session.

questions.question: What does an allowed initialize POST receive in addition to its JSON response?
options: An SSE stream but no session
A new Mcp-Session-Id header
A 204 response with no body
A permanent bearer token
questions.explanation: The initialize handler mints a 32-hex session id, stores it, and returns it in Mcp-Session-Id with HTTP 200.

questions.question: What happens to tools/list when its session id is missing or unknown?
options: It is treated as a notification
It falls back to the most recent session
It returns HTTP 404
It creates a second session implicitly
questions.explanation: Non-initialize requests must resolve an existing session; an absent or dead id is reported as HTTP 404.

questions.question: Which request header is required for the lesson's SSE GET endpoint?
options: Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Basic
Accept: text/plain
Accept: text/event-stream
questions.explanation: The streaming endpoint checks for the event-stream media type before returning SSE progress events.

questions.question: What does DELETE do for a valid session and allowed origin?
options: 204 and removes the session
It returns the full tools/list response
It keeps the session but pauses SSE
It returns HTTP 202 and schedules deletion
questions.explanation: The DELETE probe receives 204 and removes the session from SESSIONS, so subsequent requests cannot use it.

questions.question: How many progress events does the SSE probe emit?
options: One event with no token
three progress SSE events
Five events because MAX_TURNS is 5
No events; SSE is only used for errors
questions.explanation: The handler emits three progress events with progressToken p1 and total 3 before ending the stream.
